full_judgment:
2. The facts, leading to the filing of this petition, in brief, are that the petitioner herein as the preemptor filed an application for preemption under section 96 of the State Acquisition and Tenancy Act before the learned Senior Assistant Judge, Companygonj, Noakhali stating, inter alia, that he is a co-sharer tenant to the case holding by way of inheritance and purchase. Because of misunderstanding, the seller respondent No. 3, Rai Mohan Das (full brother of the preemptor) without serving any notice upon the preemptor transferred the case land to the preemptees by a registered deed of sale dated 05.06.2002. The preemptees are strangers to the case holding. After obtaining certified copy of the deed of sale the preemptor definitely came to know about the sale of the case land on 25.03.2003 and hence the case for preemption. 

 3. Respondent Nos.1 and 2 as the pre-emptees contested the preemption case by filing a written objection denying all the material statements of the application for preemption contending, inter alia, that the preemption application was not maintainable in its form. It was bad for defect of parties. The pre-emptees specific case is that before transferring the case land, seller respondent No. 3 offered the case land to the preemptor on whose refusal, a bainapatra was executed and thereafter, pre-emptee No. 1 published a legal notice through his learned lawyer in the local newspaper. As per said legal notice neither the pre-emptor nor any other co-sharer came forward to purchase the case land and in such background the seller transferred the case land to the pre-emptees by a registered deed of sale dated 05.06.2002. As such the pre-emptor waived his right of preemption by refusing to purchase the case land.
